faqs.q: Can you trap a Pittsburgh raccoon and release it in Frick Park?
faqs.a: No. Pennsylvania operator rules at 58 Pa. Code Section 147.726(g) never allow releasing a raccoon — it is a codified rabies-vector species. Pittsburgh.wildlife_intro:
Pittsburgh's calls follow its rivers and hills. Norway rats run the older rowhouse blocks, restaurant districts, and riverfront corridors from the South Side to Lawrenceville. Raccoons den in chimneys across the North Side and East End, gray squirrels work the big canopy of Squirrel Hill, Shadyside, and Mount Washington, and groundhogs burrow the city's steep, brushy hillsides and hollow edges everywhere. Bats roost in the attics of the older housing stock in every neighborhood.

The Pittsburgh calendar runs in waves. Winter drives squirrels and rodents into attics across the older housing, spring brings raccoon mothers into chimneys and soffits, and summer is bat season — Pennsylvania Game Commission guidance treats May 15 through August 1 as the maternity window, when exclusions should wait. Groundhogs dig from the first thaw until fall, when a second wave of squirrels and rodents looks for winter shelter. Our crew inspects the whole structure first, then removes the animals and seals every entry we find. The hollows matter here: wooded slopes run between neighborhoods all over the city, so a sealed house on a hollow-edge street still sits on a nightly wildlife route, and our crew seals with that in mind.
